subject: MSA + Order Form: caps, testing prohibitions, and remedies
messages:
From: Elena Mendez <elena@fintech.co>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Timothy O'Neal <tim.oneal@corpprime.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form: Limitation of Liability — benchmarking/testing carve-outs

Hi Jordan / Redwood team,

Thanks for the draft MSA and Order Form. Attached is CorpPrime's redline (MSA_Redline_CorpPrime.docx). A couple of high-level asks so we can advance internally:

- Cap: customer prefers a single-liability cap equal to 1x annual fees under the Order Form.
- Carve-outs: we need explicit carve-outs for data breaches and injunctive relief related to benchmarking/prohibited testing that harms production. We expect injunctive relief to be available without being limited by the cap.
- Prohibited testing: we are seeing vendors permit broad benchmarking / load testing language that could be used to cause service instability. We want an explicit prohibition and a remedies path (injunctive relief + potential damages for downtime caused by prohibited testing).

Please escalate anything material to your legal/product teams; we have procurement deadlines next week.

Elena

--
Elena Mendez
Senior Counsel, CorpPrime Finance
elena@fintech.co
Attachment: MSA_Redline_CorpPrime.docx (redline)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Mendez <elena@fintech.co>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Timothy O'Neal <tim.oneal@corpprime.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form: Limitation of Liability — benchmarking/testing carve-outs

Elena — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Quick response while we loop legal:

- Cap: Redwood's standard is 3x the fees or $5M (whichever is greater) for aggregate liability under the MSA. We understand CorpPrime prefers 1x; we can present a trade (lower cap in exchange for some contract protections).
- Carve-outs: we are comfortable carving out (i) IP infringement and (ii) willful misconduct from the cap. For data security incidents, we need to align on scope — Redwood maintains SOC2 controls and incident response commitments, but uncapped liability is difficult without insurance/controls alignment.
- Prohibited testing / benchmarking: we agree this needs clarity. Redwood can accept injunctive relief to stop prohibited testing (e.g., load tests run without prior notice or against prod endpoints), and we can add a clause allowing monetary damages for confirmed downtime caused by deliberate prohibited testing. We prefer to limit damages to measurable, actual loss tied to the outage rather than open-ended consequential damages.

Next steps: looping in Laura to propose precise redline language that balances both sides. If helpful, I can surface a two-option approach for your execs: (A) 3x cap with explicit uncapped carve-outs for confirmed data exfiltration and IP, or (B) 1.5x cap with stricter operational restrictions and pre-approval for any benchmarking activity.

Would you like a short call later today?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

Cc: Elena Mendez <elena@fintech.co>, Timothy O'Neal <tim.oneal@corpprime.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form: Limitation of Liability — benchmarking/testing carve-outs

Jordan / team / Elena — thanks for the context. Quick legal framing and proposed language to move the negotiation: 

1) High-level positions
- Redwood position: contract cap (3x fees or $5M) protects both parties for routine commercial risk; carve-outs for (i) gross negligence/willful misconduct, and (ii) breaches of confidentiality/data security involving unauthorized access to customer data.
- Customer position: lower cap and explicit ability to seek injunctive relief for prohibited testing that impacts production.

2) Injunctive relief vs monetary remedies
- Injunctive relief is appropriate to stop ongoing wrongful conduct (e.g., prohibited benchmarking). It's typically granted without regard to caps. Redwood can accept an explicit statement that injunctive relief remains available.
- Monetary damages for downtime caused by prohibited testing are ordinarily subject to the contract cap. To bridge, propose a narrow exception: actual, proven direct damages resulting from deliberate, unauthorized benchmarking that caused production outage shall not be limited by the cap, but only where (a) customer shows clear causation, and (b) Redwood had prior written notice or failed to disable the activity after reasonable notice. This narrows exposure while giving the customer a remedy.

3) Sample redline text (for MSA Section 10 - Limitation of Liability):
"Notwithstanding the limitation of liability set forth in this Agreement, the limitations set forth therein shall not apply to (a) damages arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) liability for bodily injury or death; and (c) damages resulting from an unauthorized access or data exfiltration event involving Customer Data proven to have occurred as a result of Redwood's breach of its obligations. In addition, if Redwood or its agents engage in deliberate, unauthorized performance testing or benchmarking against Customer's production environment that directly causes material downtime, Customer's actual, direct damages resulting from that specific incident shall not be subject to the limitation of liability, provided Customer establishes causation by a preponderance of evidence"

4) Prohibited testing / benchmarking clause (Order Form addendum):
"Customer and Vendor agree that any benchmarking, load, or stress testing that may materially impact live production services must be pre-approved in writing and conducted only on isolated non-production infrastructure. Any prohibited testing conducted by Vendor or its agents on production systems is a material breach and Customer may seek injunctive relief and damages as allowed under this Agreement."

5) Practical compromise ideas
- Offer: 2x annual fees cap + explicit SOC2 audit covenant + an operational gating clause for any benchmark testing.
- Alternative: 3x cap but include a narrowly tailored uncapped remedy only for confirmed data exfiltration (not routine outages).

I'll attach a text file with the proposed MSA language (MSA_proposed_language.txt) and an edited Order Form (OrderForm_v3.docx). Let me know if you want us to send a tracked redline for CorpPrime to review.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: MSA_proposed_language.txt; OrderForm_v3.docx
From: Elena Mendez <elena@fintech.co>

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form: Limitation of Liability — benchmarking/testing carve-outs

Laura / Jordan — appreciate the thoughtful options. A couple of quick counters from CorpPrime: 

- Cap: 1x annual fees remains our preferred commercial solution. If Redwood must have a higher cap, we will need price concessions (upfront credits / reduced per-token rates) that reflect increased vendor risk. If you are proposing 2x as a compromise, please provide the commercial offset you would expect.
- Uncapped remedies: we will accept a narrowly tailored uncapped remedy for confirmed data exfiltration. However, for prohibited benchmarking we are not comfortable carving out open-ended uncapped damages — we are instead asking that injunctive relief be explicit and automatic remedies (e.g., liquidated damages or short formula tied to minutes of downtime) be available.

Attached is our counter redline (CorpPrime_redline.docx) showing proposed language for a liquidated-damages remedy for prohibited testing: a tiered credit schedule tied to incident duration.

We can escalate pricing to our procurement lead (Tim) if Redwood makes an offer on commercial concessions tied to cap changes.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Elena Mendez
Senior Counsel, CorpPrime Finance
Attachment: CorpPrime_redline.docx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Mendez <elena@fintech.co>, Timothy O'Neal <tim.oneal@corpprime.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form: Limitation of Liability — benchmarking/testing carve-outs

Elena / Tim — thanks for the quick counter and the tiered approach in your redline. To keep this moving to procurement and exec review, here's a pragmatic path forward and concrete next steps: 

1) Commercial options for Redwood to take to execs (choose one):
  A) Liability cap = 3x annual fees (or $5M min) + 10% one-time implementation credit and 5% ongoing usage discount for first 12 months.
  B) Liability cap = 2x annual fees + 5% one-time implementation credit and 2.5% usage discount for first 12 months.
  C) Liability cap = 1.5x annual fees + no credits (only available with acceptance of the Order Form benchmark gating language and liquidated-damages schedule for prohibited testing as in your counter).

2) Legal: Laura will prepare a tracked MSA redline that includes: the narrow uncapped carve-out for confirmed data exfiltration, explicit injunctive-relief clause for prohibited testing, and the liquidated-damages schedule (if CorpPrime prefers that vs uncapped damages).

3) Ops: we will include an explicit operational runbook for approved benchmarking (pre-scheduled windows, test accounts, and throttling limits).

Next step: please confirm which commercial option your procurement prefers so I can escalate. If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min call today with finance and legal.

Jordan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
